subject: general
question: A shopkeeper gives 20% commission on the retail price of one article and earns 5% profit. If his commission is reduced by 10%, then what is his approximate profit percentage? (Nearest integral value)
solution:
**GIVEN:**

Commission is 20% on the retail price of one article

Profit is 5%

**FORMULA USED:**

C.P. = 100/(100 + P%) × S.P. 

Profit = S.P. - C.P. 

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100

Where, S.P. = Selling price, C.P. = Cost price 

**CALCULATION:**

Let us assume retail price of one article be 100x 

S.P. after 20% commission = 100x× 80/100 = 80x

Also, Profit% = 5%

Now, C.P. = 100/(100 + 5) × 80x

⇒ 100/105 × 80X = 76.19x

Now, according to the given question when commission becomes 10% of retail price

Then, S.P. = 100x × 90/100 = 90x 

Profit = S.P. - C.P. 

⇒ 90x - 76.19x = 13.81x

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.)× 100

⇒ (13.81x /76.19x)× 100 = 18.12% ≈ 18% [nearest integer value]

**Hence, approximate profit% is 18% **
